::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.card .h-100 .text-center}
::: {.card-header}
**Assignment**
:::
::: {.card-body}
![](/images/noun_Four_2010371.png){fig-alt="Assignment" width=80px}

The editorial office assigns the manuscript to the AEA Data Editor, using the "ScholarOne" (ex-Manuscript Central) system.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.card .h-100 .text-center}
::: {.card-header}
**Verification**
:::
::: {.card-body}
![](/images/noun_five_2010369.png){fig-alt="Verification" width=80px}

The AEA Data Editor team downloads materials from openICPSR, [conducts reproducibility checks](https://social-science-data-editors.github.io/guidance/Verification_guidance.html), and then writes a [report](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/replication-template/blob/master/REPLICATION.md). **This happens without interaction with the authors.** If changes need to be made, the report is communicated to the authors, who make changes and re-submit, the cycle repeating until the replication package is deemed acceptable.
:::
::: {.card-footer}
[**Learn more »**](/reproducibility-checks.qmd){.stretched-link}
:::
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4}
::: {.card .h-100 .text-center}
::: {.card-header}
**Forthcoming**
:::
::: {.card-body}
![](/images/noun_Check_3836232.png){fig-alt="Forthcoming" width=80px}

The acceptance report (possibly with some minor additional changes) is communicated to the editorial office and the Editor of the journal. This starts the copy-editing process, and at this time, the manuscript becomes "**forthcoming**." Small changes can still be incorporated at this stage. As soon as the replication package is completed, it is published. The manuscript is published once copy-edited and scheduled to an issue.
:::
:::
:::

:::
